routes.description: Infer a supernatural, intelligent, and moral creator from features of reality, then connect that creator specifically to the biblical God through Jesus.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its causal, design, and moral inferences establish the relevant divine attributes and the Jesus evidence supplies the biblical identification.

motionBridge.description: The inferred creator must be identified with the God of the Bible rather than only an unspecified supernatural cause.

centralBridges.description: The universe's existence and beginning must require a cause beyond physical matter.
Fine-tuning and complex functional organization must warrant an inference to intelligence.
Objective moral obligations must require a personal moral source beyond naturalistic preference.
The historical case concerning Jesus must support resurrection and divine identity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Human fallibility must remain compatible with knowledge of burden-relevant foundational truths.
Suffering must be compatible with divine goodness through a coherent redemptive or ultimate account.

routes.description: Withhold the biblical-theist conclusion by showing that natural explanations, evidential limits, religious diversity, and suffering undercut its necessary inferences.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative evidence does not discriminate the biblical God from natural alternatives, uncertainty, rival religions, or unsupported supernatural claims.

motionBridge.description: The total evidence must fail to justify the existence and specifically biblical identity asserted in the motion.

centralBridges.description: Confidence in supernatural claims must remain proportioned to testable and publicly available support.
Causation, biological complexity, morality, and apparent design must admit nondivine explanations or remain unresolved.
Biblical revelation and resurrection claims must withstand comparison with informed disagreement and rival traditions.
Apparently gratuitous innocent suffering must be reconciled with the claimed omnipotent and benevolent God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Finite human access to objective truth must warrant intellectual humility and revisability.
Methodological naturalism must provide a workable standard for detecting causal interaction and comparing explanations.

sectionSelections.title: Knowledge and Evidential Standards
sectionSelections.rationale: The permissible degree of certainty and the testability of supernatural claims govern how every substantive inference in the debate can bear the motion-level burden.

proSelections.proposition: Inquiry should follow rational argument wherever it leads without imposing a prior barrier against nonmaterial conclusions.
Human fallibility and probabilistic caution do not preclude certainty about some truths or require every claim about God to remain permanently uncertain.

conSelections.proposition: Because human beings are fallible, confidence should be probabilistic and proportioned to a claim's prior plausibility and supporting evidence.
A supernatural claim protected from every possible test is empirically indistinguishable from the nonexistence of its alleged object.

sectionSelections.title: Cosmic Causation
sectionSelections.rationale: The first-cause inference is an independent path from the universe to a nonphysical creator, while objections contest whether the regress identifies any God.

proSelections.proposition: Because every material effect requires a cause and the universe began, the universe requires a supernatural cause.
Physical matter cannot cause the universe's own existence, so the cause required by physical effects must be nonphysical.

conSelections.proposition: The first-cause argument does not establish God because exempting God from causation is special pleading and the regress may end in an unknown or uncaused universe.

sectionSelections.title: Fine-Tuning and Biological Design
sectionSelections.rationale: The design dispute determines whether cosmic parameters and functional biological organization supply evidence of intelligence or remain explicable without a supernatural designer.

proSelections.proposition: The universe's fine-tuning and life's complex functional organization require an intelligent designer.
Complex functional information and integrated biological structures can indicate intelligent origin even when the designer is not directly observed.

conSelections.proposition: Biological complexity does not establish a supernatural designer because natural selection is an observable bottom-up process that produces functional adaptations.
Fine-tuning arguments infer design from unresolved physics and therefore do not constitute established evidence for God.

sectionSelections.title: Moral Objectivity and Natural Origins
sectionSelections.rationale: The grounding of objective moral standards bears on whether reality requires a personal moral God or whether morality can arise and function within naturalism.

proSelections.proposition: Objective moral values exist and require a personal moral God rather than a purely material reality.
Evolutionary cooperation yields self-interest, social preference, and variable behavior rather than objectively binding moral standards.

conSelections.proposition: Objective morality can be grounded in sentient well-being, reduced suffering, flourishing, and bodily autonomy without divine commands.
Objective-seeming morality arose through social-primate evolution, reciprocal cooperation, detection of exploiters, and internalized virtuous habits rather than divine command.

sectionSelections.title: Jesus, Resurrection, and Religious Diversity
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue supplies the required bridge from generic theism to the biblical God and tests that identification against resurrection scrutiny and competing religious claims.

proSelections.proposition: Jesus's exceptional moral character, crucifixion, reported resurrection appearances, and followers' sacrifices identify him with the biblical God.
Religious disagreement does not defeat Christianity because consensus is not a truth test, some Jews accept Jesus, Christianity arose among Jews, and rival scriptures can be compared evidentially.

conSelections.proposition: Competing religions make similarly confident claims of inspired revelation, so confidence in the Bible alone cannot establish its divine authority.
The resurrection's extraordinary character does not make it credible, and its historical support is too weak when comparable miracle claims are rejected despite testimony.

sectionSelections.title: Suffering and Divine Goodness
sectionSelections.rationale: The compatibility of innocent suffering with omnipotent benevolence bears directly on the asserted biblical God's attributes and on possible redemptive or afterlife explanations.

proSelections.proposition: Suffering does not logically disprove a loving God because Christ's suffering illustrates how presently unexplained pain can precede salvation and an ultimately redemptive outcome.
Personal suffering does not entail God's nonexistence because suffering may draw people toward God and be rectified in an eternal afterlife.

conSelections.proposition: Apparently gratuitous natural suffering, including childhood leukemia, conflicts with an omnipotent and benevolent God when moral growth could occur without devastating innocent people.
